t: Spain’s richest viceroyalty, ruled from Mexico City over Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and the Philippines.
Its silver, coined as the Spanish dollar and carried by the Manila galleons, linked Europe, the Americas and China.
Hidalgo’s revolt of 1810 began a long war, and the Plan of Iguala and Treaty of Córdoba ended Spanish rule in 1821.
dyk: The Manila galleons sailed between Acapulco and Manila for 250 years, from 1565 to 1815, carrying Mexican silver to Asia and returning with Chinese silk and porcelain.
ev: Tenochtitlan falls to Hernán Cortés and his indigenous allies
Antonio de Mendoza becomes the first viceroy of New Spain
The Manila galleon route links Acapulco with the Philippines
The Jesuits are expelled during the Bourbon reforms
Miguel Hidalgo launches the war of independence at Dolores
The Plan of Iguala and the Treaty of Córdoba end Spanish rule

f.founder: Hernán Cortés (conquest); Antonio de Mendoza (first viceroy)
